THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 02.12.2019 passed by 3rd Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and VI MACT, Davanagere (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.291/2019.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under; One Sri.Anand was traveling in his car bearing Registration No.KA.16/N.7027 on 31.01.2019 when his car reached near Pijnara Hegdal Village,
Hagaribommanahalli NC: 2024:KHC:15014 Town, the driver of the car drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner while overtaking the lorry took the car to left side of the road due to which left door opened and Anand fell down from the car and succumbed to the injuries.
The claimants, who are the unfortunate widow and her minor children, filed the claim petition seeking compensation along with the mother of the deceased.

3.1. On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were placed exparte and respondent No.3- Insurance company filed statement of objections, denying claims of the claimant including age,
avocation, income of the deceased
also averred that the driver of the car did not hold proper and valid driving license and violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, sought for absolving the liability of the Insurance-company.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P9.

On the other hand,
respondents neither examined any witness nor got marked any documents.

3.4. On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.12,85,000/- with interest @ 9% p.a and has directed respondent no.3 - Insurance Company to deposit compensation amount within a period of 30 days.
3.5.
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

4. The main contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants is that, the tribunal has committed an NC: 2024:KHC:15014 error in awarding meager compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, she seeks enhancement of compensation.

Smt Uma J vs Suresh R on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61108067/
3
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has rightly awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.

Therefore,
on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondent No.3- Insurance Company and perused the impugned judgment and award and the documents at Exs.P1 to P4.
As per the police records at Exs.P1 to P4, the FIR and Charge sheet are laid against the driver of the Car, which is not challenged before any court of law.
Hence, negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending Car.
Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and the appropriate multiplier for awarding compensation.
It is seen that the deceased Sri.Anand was aged 36 years as on the date of occurrence of accident and the appropriate multiplier would be '15' which is correctly taken by the tribunal.
It does not call for interference.
Tribunal has taken the income of Rs.9,000/- p.m whereas, the notional income as per the chart prepared by the legal service authority for the year, 2019 is Rs.14,000/- p.m.
Hence, income is taken as Rs.14,000/- p.m.
As they are 4 dependants 1/4th is deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Which does not call for interference.

8. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellants that the tribunal failed to award future prospects, as the deceased was aged less than 40 year, 40% would have to be added towards future prospects to the income.

The income as taken as Rs. 14,000/-p.m, NC: 2024:KHC:15014 40%
would have to be added towards.

Loss of dependency as under (14,000 + 40% = 19,600/- / 4=
4,900/- * 14700 * 12 * 15 = 26,46,000/-) as against 12,15,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
9.
Learned counsel for the respondent/corporation contends that the tribunal has committed a gross error in awarding Rs.2,15,000/- towards consortium to the claimants 1 to 3 which is highly exorbitant.

As contemplated in the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, would be awarded and in view of this court enhancing the compensation, the consortium amounted awarded exorbitant could be reduced.

sentences.text: The submission made by learned counsel for the respondent is accepted.

Towards loss of consortium, the tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- which is on the lower side for the first appellant and Rs.40,000/- for the appellant Nos.1 and 4, whereas each of the claimants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- per person in consonance to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethis case.

Therefore, in all they would be entitled to Rs.1,60,000/-
(Rs.40,000 x 4) with an 10% escalation for 1 block period, which is an addition of Rs.16,000/-.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled to Rs.1,76,000/- under this head.
